problem_description: Compute the radius of gyration in nm of the 50-bead linear uncharged polymer. The nonbonded dispersion interactions were modeled using the Lennard–Jones (LJ) potential, with the bead size parameter 𝜎 = 0.40 nm and the interaction energyparameter 𝜀 = 1.0 kJ mol−1. The polymer has harmonic bonds of 0.153 nm with a force constant of 330,000 kJ/mol·nm² and harmonic angles of 111° with a force constant of 100 kJ/mol·rad². Lorentz–Berthelot mixing rules were employed to model the unlike interactions. The polymer chain was solvated with SPC/E water molecules in a cubic simulation box of 5.03 nm with periodic boundary conditions. The energy minimization should be performed using the steepest-descent algorithm with energy minimization steps of 0.01 nm and 50,000 steps. NVT equilibration should be performed followed by energy minimization for 20 ps using the Nose-Hoover thermostat. The NPT equilibration should maintained the temperature and pressure using the Nose–Hoover thermostat and Parrinello–Rahman barostat, respectively, with damping coefficients of 𝜏𝑇 = 0.5 ps and 𝜏𝑃 = 2.0 ps for 1000 steps at 1 bar pressure. During the equilibration position restrain should be used (define=-DPOSRES_B). A production runs (10,000 steps) must be performed using the same thermostate (tau_t = 1.0 nm) and the barostat as NPT equlibration while keeping the same parameter. A cutoff distance of 1.0 nm was employed to compute the van der Waals interactions, while electrostatic interactions were calculated using the Particle Mesh Ewald (PME) method with a grid spacing of 0.12 nm and a real-space cutoff radius of 1.0 nm. The bond lengths of the solute molecules were constrained using the LINCS algorithm.
